negative_reviews.author: Under.Concrete
negative_reviews.text:
Staff were very friendly and helpful, clearly putting a lot of effort in and it made us feel very welcome. Ground floor seating was a bit uncomfortable, quite a few tables close together so somewhat noisy and you feel a bit like you're in a corridor especially if your back is facing the area people are walking through. We got the lunch deal which was very reasonably priced and promised to arrive in under thirty minutes (good if you're in a rush). It did arrive quite promptly.
For the speed and price I think you get what you'd expect for the food. It's about average in most places though the vegan chicken used in the Vegan Chicken Katsu was notably a bit cardboardy.
Come for quick, reliable, and reasonably priced food but don't expect it to rival the quality of food from independent Japanese restaurants in the area.

negative_reviews.text: Service was better than the food and atmosphere. Aydin served us, he was a great guy and very friendly. If there is one reason to go back would be for Aydin.

negative_reviews.author: Mamnoon
negative_reviews.text: Came here because of all the glowing reviews. Just finished my food and I feel immense disappointment. I got the beef steak ramen (the halal version) and my friend got the miso chicken ramen. The broth was an embarrassment. In fact if you told me that it was water with some salt and soy sauce added I would have believed it. The meat portion was small, but the overall dish did leave me feeling full. But the overall lack of any depth or taste in the broth took away from any possible satisfaction that the fullness could've given me. I also got takoyaki which in all fairness was decent. Also having to use the QR code over and over again to order refills for our water is a bit dark in my humble opinion. The only thing positive about the place is how quick they got the food to us and the pretty location and seating. So if you're here for the aesthetics this is the place for you. But if you're here expecting decent food please don't bother. The pictures are decieving.

negative_reviews.author: LP Y
negative_reviews.text:
A complete disaster from drinks to food.

The Matcha Scam: I ordered a matcha latte based on the beautiful, vibrant green pictures in the menu (as seen in image). What I actually received was a muddy brown drink with zero hint of green. Charging 6.5 for total false advertising is a scam.

The Awful Tempura: The food was just as disappointing. The tempura was incredibly greasy, soggy, and coated in a ridiculously thick layer of batter. Real tempura is supposed to be light and crispy, but this felt like thick flour dough dropped in oil. One bite and my mouth was literally pooling with grease.

negative_reviews.author: Neil Janke
negative_reviews.text: I've visited a few times and always enjoyed the experience. The food is delicious, and the service is excellent. My only suggestion would be regarding the music. I think traditional Japanese music would complement the atmosphere much better than the current urban pop music, which feels a little out of place.

negative_reviews.author: C
negative_reviews.text:
We have visited Maki & Ramen five times now, and unfortunately the level of service has been very inconsistent. Our visit yesterday was by far the worst and has left us deciding not to return.

We were a family of five, and I joined the group shortly after finishing work. We asked if we could move from our table to an available booth as it offered more space for our party. We were told this was not possible because our food order had already been assigned to the table and we would need to wait until all the food had arrived before moving. This made little sense to us as the booth was directly next to our table.

What made the situation more frustrating was that the booth was later given to a group of three, while our party of five had to squeeze around two small tables with dishes balanced across them. With a bill of around £120, I would expect a better level of customer service and a little more flexibility where possible.

In addition, the member of staff we spoke to had a very noticeable body odour, which was unfortunately apparent whenever food was brought to the table. I appreciate this may be an uncomfortable issue to raise, but when customers are dining, hygiene and presentation are important parts of the experience.

Throughout the meal, no one checked whether we were okay despite the obvious lack of space, and no effort was made to revisit the request or offer any alternative solution. After visiting several times previously, it is disappointing that our final experience was so poor.

The food itself was enjoyable, but the service and overall experience left a very negative impression. Sadly, after five visits, we will not be returning.

negative_reviews.text: mid.

negative_reviews.author: EMG
negative_reviews.text: I want to preface my review of this restaurant by giving a mention to the two very welcoming staff members who were the reason my friend and I made the visit to Maki Nori. The staff were great, I can’t fault the service and the atmosphere inside was warm and provides a space that a real omakase restaurant does but I can’t help but feel there was a bit of false advertisement going on. The food was nothing special. My friend and I got the 15 piece ‘omakase’ but it came all on one plate? The quality of fish was so average and borderline not fresh, but it might have been different for the more expensive cuts of fish like the Chutoro tuna that I saw other people order. The fish that featured on the ‘omakase’ set was average at best - we were really surprised when it arrived. The lemon zest on the salmon nigiri added nothing and seemed like an attempt to fancify a simple item that needed no embellishment had the fish quality been at a certain standard. To provide a comparison, Eat Tokyo’s quality of fish is much better and sits at a better price range but I guess the atmosphere is something new…
